### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-cluster`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs/:ref (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataClusterBridgePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), originNode (symbol, a field of interface ClusterConnectorCredentialMutationPayload))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_MUTATION_CLUSTER_CHANNEL (symbol, a top-level const object), ClusterConnectorCredentialMutationPayload (symbol, a top-level interface; a top-level type), MetadataClusterBridgePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), originNode (symbol, a field of interface ClusterConnectorCredentialMutationPayload), /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs/:ref (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via MetadataClusterBridgePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), attachClusterPubSub (symbol, a method of interface ConnectorCredentialDoor))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `57a7b229611cee9904d297a226cc34d318dfa18b` — the merge of head `8b40e4fa254306912fb197fe434a91157d9c7937` into base `ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 57a7b229611cee9904d297a226cc34d318dfa18b && git checkout 57a7b229611cee9904d297a226cc34d318dfa18b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 8b40e4fa254306912fb197fe434a91157d9c7937 && git checkout -B drift-repro ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 && git merge --no-ff 8b40e4fa254306912fb197fe434a91157d9c7937

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #27941 · head `8b40e4fa254306912fb197fe434a91157d9c7937` · 2026-10-30T05:05Z

## 维护者速读

When the credential door (`PUT|DELETE /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs/:ref`) writes or clears a connector credential on one replica, the replica now publishes an address-only message on the cluster lane `connector-credential.mutated`. The payload is `{ originNode, ref }` and never carries a value. Every other replica then reconciles its declared connectors on its reconcile queue and re-reads the shared row. A connector that was held on a peer recovers without a reload. Before this, only the replica that took the request recovered. This implements ruling 6513279565 (letter A, attached at A1): the fourth duck-typed lane in `MetadataClusterBridgePlugin`, with a row in `cluster.mdx` §6.2. There is no synthetic `metadata.mutated` and no polling. Single-replica and `memory`-driver deployments are unchanged.

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** draft → main, `Fixes #27428`.
  - Eight files across `service-automation` (door publish, receiver, channel constant, engine seam), `service-cluster` (lane 4), the §6.2 row, tests and a changeset.
  - `check-governed-merges --pr 27941`: NOT governed, +672 / −17.
  - File surface as claimed.
- **Read of the diff:**
  - The publish happens only after a successful `store.set` or `store.clear`, as a best-effort `warn` on failure.
  - The receiver drops its own `originNode` and ignores an empty `ref`.
  - The receiver runs `materializeDeclaredConnectors`, which is the serialized `onReconcileQueue` wrapper around `reconcileDeclaredConnectors`.
  - Attach is idempotent on `(pubsub, nodeId)` and is detached at `destroy()`.
  - Nothing new is exported from the package root.
- **Seat ruling on the open question:** `Clause-②: no` stands. `AutomationEngine.attachConnectorCredentialPubSub` is an internal duck-typed seam between two server packages, the same pattern as `attachDatasourceMutationPubSub` and `attachAuthzInvalidationPubSub`. It widens no published accept set, so no contract review is owed. `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch on both packages.
- **Tests:**
  - A two-kernel pin over one SQLite store and one shared bus was red on the base, 5 of 5. Three ablations each go red where declared.
  - Six bridge lane-4 cases cover the memory skip, a throwing attach that leaves lanes 1 to 3 up, and detach on shutdown.
  - `service-automation` 2808/2808 and `service-cluster` 111/111 (os-dev-report 6515174220).
- **Serial:** draft #27819 also edits `service-automation/src/plugin.ts`. This head already merged `main`, and whichever of the two lands later merges `main` again.
- **Out of scope, per the ruling:** whether a published connector change materialises only on the publishing replica. It gets its own card once measured.
- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 50 total, 38 success, 12 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Landing:** Tier S, under the maintainer's landing grant for this term (2026-10-29 22:05Z, seat thread). Ready + auto-merge through the relay.

**ACCEPT**
